data.name: Magniel
data.gender_notes: Magniel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Magen, which means 'shield' or 'protector'. In the Bible, Magniel could symbolize a strong believer who feels protected by God and offers magnificent services to the Lord. Or, it may be the name of a warrior in the army of God. The name Magniel carries the meaning “Magnificent God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Magniel usually hope their child will grow to embody magnificent god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing faith and trust in the protective power of God.
data.etymology: Magniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Magnificent God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Magniel total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: מַגְנִיאֵל
in_hebrew.meaning: בעל היופי, העצום, הנשמה, הקודש, המלאך
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם בעברית, 'מַגְנִיאֵל', פירושו 'בעל היופי, העצום, הנשמה, הקודש, המלאך'. השם נזכר באגדות ובביבליוגרפיות. בתקופה הביזנטית, השם 'מגניאל' היה נפוץ. נחשבו לבעלי כבוד, אדיבים, ועצמאיים. פעם, השם 'מגניאל' היה יוצא מן הכלל, אבל הוא אינו יוצא מן הכלל יותר.

in_greek.name: Μαγνιήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα 'Μαγνιήλ' προέρχεται από το Εβραϊκό 'מַגְנִיאֵל', που σημαίνει 'ὑπερφυής, μεγαλοπρεπής, θείος, ἄγγελος'. Στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη, ο 'Μαγνιήλ' ήταν ο αρχάγγελος που παρέσυσε τον Αμράν, πατέρα του Αμσαλ. Βρέθηκε επίσης στο 'Βιβλίο του Εnoch'. Στη Βυζαντινή εποχή, το όνομα 'Μαγνιήλ' ήταν phổуляρ. Οι έμποροι και οι έμποροι πίστευαν ότι οι άνθρωποι με το όνομα 'Μαγνιήλ' ήταν ιδιαίτερα ευτυχισμένοι.

in_latin.name: Magniel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen 'Magniel' originem habet ex Hebraico 'magniel', quod significat 'magnificus, fortis, angelus'. In Veteri Testamento, 'Magniel' erat archangelus qui interfecit Amran, patrem Amshalem. Inscriptus est etiam in 'Liber Enoch'. In aetate Byzantina, nomen 'Magniel' erat in usu. Mercatores et mercatores credebant quod homines cum nomen 'Magniel' erant maxime felices.

in_english.name: Magniel
in_english.meaning: magnificent, strong, angelic, one who is powerful and majestic
in_english.long_meaning: The name Magniel originates from the Hebrew name 'magniel', which means 'magnificent, strong, angelic, one who is powerful and majestic'. In the Bible, Magniel was the archangel who slew Amram, the father of Amshal. He is also found in the Book of Enoch. In Byzantine times, the name Magniel was popular among merchants and traders, who believed that people with the name Magniel were exceptionally fortunate.

data.cultural_impact: The name Magniel originated from Hebrew culture and has a rich heritage. It is a unique name that stands out from the crowd.
data.spiritual_significance: In biblical times, a Magniel was a protector or guardian, often serving as a warrior in the army of God. The name represents a deep faith and trust in the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Magniel: From the Hebrew name Magnal, meaning "mighty," and the Latin suffix -iel, meaning "God is my light." This name symbolizes the belief in God's strength and guidance illuminating one's path in life.

biblical_reference.note: There is no direct reference to the name Magniel in the Bible. However, the name is mentioned in the Book of Enoch, which is part of the Old Testament Apocrypha.

historical_references.reference: Magnus Ericson, also known as Magnus the Good, was a legendary Norse chieftain and the traditional founder of Iceland. He is believed to have led the first Norse settlements in Iceland around 870 AD.
historical_references.context: Norse mythology and early Icelandic history

historical_references.reference: Saint Magnus of Orkney, a Christian bishop and martyr, was the bishop of the Orkney Islands. He was killed by the Earl Harald Maddadsson in 1111 AD, and his death led to the eventual Christianization of the islands.
historical_references.context: Early Christianity in Scotland and the Orkney Islands
